locator.text: Equation (9.18), p. 113, in the statement of Lemma 9.8

evidence: paper: |\mathscr{R}(u^{[j]},p^{[j]})|_m \le C_{j,m}\, q^{h\sigma_j-K_m}\,(1+|\log q|)^{P_{j,m}} + E_{j,m},\qquad E_{j,m} \le C_{j,m,N}\, q^{N}\ \text{for every } N

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. The Lean bound drops two things the display allows: the logarithmic factor (1+|log q|)^{P_{j,m}} and the additive flat error E_{j,m}. It asserts ‖D^k R(u^{[J]},p^{[J]})‖ ≤ C q^{hσ_J-K_m} outright, for every k ≤ m, on the whole domain. That implies the printed display: take P_{j,m} = 0, so (1+|log q|)^{P} = 1, and E_{j,m} = 0, which satisfies E_{j,m} ≤ C_{j,m,N} q^N for every N with C = 0. Nothing in (9.18) is lost — the implication runs from the Lean statement to the paper's. The source docstrings say the same ('all flat remainders are absorbed, so its additional flat-error term can be chosen to be zero'; 'The excluded flat errors have already been estimated at the same power and included in this bound'), and that absorption is a claim about the proofs, which I did not trace. The residual operator matches the paper's R(u,p) = ∂_t u + (u·∇)u − Δu + ∇p (p. 115) term by term at viscosity one, and σ_J = 1/5 + J/10 is exactly the paper's σ_j of (9.8); K_m = paperJetLoss B N0 m carries no stage index, as 'with K_m independent of j' requires. Norm and domain encodings are as for (9.17).
